title: Implement add command
description: Implement the add subcommand: parse <text>, optional --source, optional --meta KEY=VALUE repeatable args, auto-init DB if not present, embed text via _embed, generate UUID v4, wrap both inserts (memories + memories_vec using lastrowid) in a single transaction, print 'Added <uuid>'.
acceptance_criteria: ./memory.py add 'hello world' prints 'Added <uuid>' where uuid is a valid UUID v4
Two add calls with different text produce two distinct UUIDs
Both memories and memories_vec tables contain a matching row after add
Running add without prior init auto-initialises the DB
--source and --meta flags are stored in the memories row
A simulated failure after the memories insert (e.g. bad vec insert) leaves the DB unchanged (transaction rolled back)

handoff_summary.risks: The memories table uses TEXT id (UUID) while memories_vec uses rowid for the FK link — this relies on SQLite rowid matching lastrowid immediately after INSERT, which is correct for single-connection sequential inserts.
handoff_summary.next_action: Run tester agent to validate acceptance criteria.
handoff_summary.conflict_risks: No conflicts expected; cmd_add was a stub with no sibling bead edits to this function.
handoff_summary.design_decisions: Used `with conn:` context manager for automatic transaction commit/rollback. memories_vec rowid is linked to memories.rowid via lastrowid immediately after the memories INSERT — this is safe for single-connection sequential writes. The `conn.close()` is in a finally block to ensure cleanup.
handoff_summary.test_coverage_notes: Tester should verify: UUID v4 format, two distinct UUIDs on two calls, both table rows present, auto-init, --source/--meta persistence, and rollback on vec insert failure.
handoff_summary.known_limitations: No deduplication — identical text will create multiple distinct entries. This is by design per the spec.
